newsitem.title: FRANCE: No grain export bids in France, as season ends.
newsitem.headline: No grain export bids in France, as season ends.

text.p: Grain traders made no export bids through France at the European Union's last weekly export tender of the season on Thursday, an ONIC cereals official said.
Traders had not expected significant bidding, but the lack of any bids at all through France reflects the fact the EU has already virtually closed down the campaign early, traders said.
"End of story," said one trader of the 1996/97 campaign.
It was not immediately whether there were any bids for barley exports through other member states, but Germany, which often handles such bids, was closed for a public holiday.
Thursday's weekly grain meeting in Brussels is likely to be dominated instead by preferential maize imports to Spain.
The European Commission last week rejected all bids for cuts in its usual tariff for non-EU maize imported to Spain, but increased the amount open for bidding by 300,000 tonnes.
The allocation for tariff cuts is now 800,000 tonnes.

Bids for the tariff reductions are considered by the EU's cereals management committee. The tariff cuts apply to non-EU maize but in practice they are awarded for imports from the United States under a 1987 trade deal compensating Washington for trade losses when Spain and Portugal joined the EU.
